name: Livestock Evaluation & Judging

objectives.text: Identify the main external body parts of a cow, pig, sheep, and goat such as the head, shoulder, back, loin, rump, and legs
Identify signs that a farm animal is healthy and well fed such as bright eyes, a smooth coat, good body fill, and steady walking
Identify common breeds of beef cattle, swine, sheep, and goats by color pattern, ear set, head shape, and other breed characteristics
Explain how an animal's structure, including its feet, legs, pasterns, and topline, affects its ability to move freely and stay sound
Compare two animals for muscling by observing thickness through the forearm, loin, stifle, and hindquarter
Classify livestock by frame size, degree of muscling, and body condition score
Use standard livestock evaluation terminology to describe the differences between two animals in a pair
Place a class of four livestock animals from most to least desirable and give at least one reason for each pair in the placing
Describe the ideal market type for steers, barrows, market lambs, and market goats in terms of muscle, finish, balance, and structural correctness based on industry standards
Record organized judging notes on a class that capture the key comparisons and grants for each pair
Evaluate breeding females and males for reproductive soundness, including udder and underline quality, testicular development, and structural correctness
Justify the selection of a project animal for a supervised agricultural experience based on evaluation criteria, project goals, and budget
Estimate carcass traits such as backfat thickness, loin eye area, and yield grade from visual appraisal of live market animals
Analyze an animal's structural correctness, muscling, finish, and breed character to develop a set of oral reasons defending a judging placement
Answer a judge's questions about a livestock class by recalling specific observed differences among the animals
Analyze how differences in muscling, finish, soundness, and reproductive potential affect the economic value of market and breeding animals
Rank a class of breeding animals by combining visual appraisal with performance data such as expected progeny differences and weights
Evaluate a class of market or breeding animals using industry evaluation criteria and deliver organized oral reasons that justify the final placing
Design a practice livestock judging class with an official placing, cuts, and a model set of oral reasons

changes: Kept and reworded all six original objectives. Added competencies for anatomy, breed identification, muscling comparison, judging terminology, ideal market type, note taking, reproductive soundness of breeding stock, SAE project selection, live carcass estimation, questions classes, economic value, performance data classes, and designing practice classes. Linked standards only for grades 9 to 12 where they fit.
